name: toast
title: Toast
purpose: Present transient, non-blocking notifications in a viewport-level managed stack.
useFor: Recoverable errors with a concise action
avoidFor: Information required to complete a form
accessibility: Non-destructive items use polite status semantics while destructive items use assertive alert semantics.
The viewport never moves focus and Escape dismisses the newest dismissible toast.
Timers pause for hover, focus, window blur, and hidden documents so actions remain reachable.
commonMistakes: Using Toast for feedback a user must retain.
Adding several unrelated actions to one toast.
Using a short duration for long descriptions or keyboard actions.

examples.title: Success notification
examples.description: A polite success item confirms a completed background action.
examples.source:
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from "vue";
import Button from "@/components/ui/Button.vue";
import ToastViewport, { type ToastItem } from "@/components/ui/ToastViewport.vue";

const notifications = ref<readonly ToastItem[]>([]);
let sequence = 0;

function notify(): void {
  sequence += 1;
  notifications.value = [
    ...notifications.value,
    {
      id: `notification-${sequence}`,
      title: "Notification heading placeholder",
      description: "Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit.",
      color: "success",
      variant: "surface",
      size: "md",
      rounded: "lg",
      duration: 5000,
      sticky: true,
      dismissible: true,
      actionLabel: "Undo placeholder",
    },
  ];
}
</script>

<template>
  <Button @click="notify">Show notification placeholder</Button>
  <ToastViewport
    v-model="notifications"
    position="bottom-end"
    @action="(item) => console.info(item.id)"
  />
</template>
